summary: Bradford's parks and environment positions center on expanding and maintaining recreation infrastructure, protecting green space and ravines, and advancing climate measures like EV charging and district energy. Bradford opposes closing recreation facilities such as Weston Arena and Dentonia Park Golf Course, and instead supports building "net new" facilities including dedicated pickleball courts, cricket pitches, splash pads, and a disc golf course. Bradford emphasizes "back to basics" service delivery—open pools, clean parks, functioning washrooms, lifeguard staffing—and frames recent City failures as accountability problems rather than budget shortfalls. Bradford supports Toronto's net-zero-by-2040 target, EV charging expansion, tree canopy growth, and ravine protection (notably Small's Creek). Bradford opposes encampments in parks, the toboggan ban, and what is characterized as a tree-equity policy distraction. Bradford supports the alcohol-in-parks pilot, ActiveTO, and protecting waterfront use including a motorized watercraft exclusion zone at Woodbine Beach.
